edbDesc: A pyrophoric substance ignites spontaneously in air at or below 55 degrees centigrade. The creation of sparks from metals is based on the pyrophoricity of small metal particles. The sparking mechanism in cigarette lighters is an example. Some liquids and gases are phyrophoric.
title: Pyrophoricity
description: Some materials burst into flame by themselves the moment they touch air, usually finely powdered metals or very reactive chemicals. Scraping a hard cerium-iron alloy flings off tiny shavings that ignite instantly, the spark of a lighter flint; Carl Auer von Welsbach patented this ferrocerium in 1903. Rocket engines use pyrophoric liquids to light their fuel without a spark plug.
effect: a substance catches fire by itself on contact with air
usedIn: Ferrocerium lighter flints and fire-starter rods
Triethylborane igniter in the SR-71's engines and SpaceX Merlin engines
strength: Ferrocerium sparks burn at about 3,000°C, and triethylborane ignites in air even at -20°C.
pickWhy: Borderline: Judgment call on date: no single discoverer (Homberg described a self-igniting powder around 1711; Auer von Welsbach made it useful in 1903), so year and discoverer left null; the effect itself is a clear keep.
